key_insight: Rice husk ash can be converted into silica powder that is amorphous after 800 °C treatment and crystallizes into quartz/cristobalite after annealing at 1200 °C, making it suitable as a thermal-spray feedstock.
engineering_relevance: This provides a low-cost, bio-derived route to silica powders with tunable phase structure for coating and thermal spray applications.
method: Chemical treatment of rice husk ash to extract silica
Heat treatment at 800 °C for 3 h to obtain amorphous SiO2
evidence_signal: XRD confirmed amorphous silica at 800 °C and the emergence of quartz and cristobalite after 1200 °C annealing, while FTIR showed Si–O–Si and hydroxyl bands and laser diffraction measured D50 ≈ 88.9 μm.
watch_item: The relatively large median particle size and phase changes during high-temperature annealing may require further milling and process control before consistent thermal-spray deposition.
paper_title: Synthesis of Amorphous and Crystalline Silicon Dioxide Powder Composites from Rice Husk Ash for Thermal Spray Deposit
